messages:
maya: planning a maintenance window THU 03:00-05:00 UTC for apac-west1 and eu-west2 — NIC firmware + rolling node reboots. we'll do cohorted drains (10% pools) to avoid global capacity hits. expect ~5-8 min per node drain/reboot.

liam: rough impact on GPU capacity for Dedicated customers? any customers on reserved pools in apac that we should whittle away from?

maya: Dedicated pools in apac are light but a few high-commit tenants in eu-west2. plan: prioritize draining non-reserved cohorts first, then stagger reserved ones at end of window. fallback routing -> hosted for latency-tolerant jobs.

ethan: apac capacity is already thin mid-nite. recommend pre-warming two hot standby pools in us-east1 for cross-region spill. that will increase cost for the night (~$800/night) but keeps SLOs.

maya: noted — cost estimate ok if we keep it to 2 pools. ops: can we do auto-backfill thresholds at 20% free to avoid triggering large reroutes?

liam: yes, set policy: if free_capacity < 20% for pool -> block further scheduled drains and notify oncall. also enable route-weight shift to us-east1 with 10s ramp.

ethan: also: KV cache warmup is important after reboots. please add a warmup job to seed prefixes for top 50 tenants in each affected pool. otherwise cold starts will tank latency.

maya: good call. here's the drain command and warmup snippet I'll run:
```
kubectl cordon $NODE && kubectl drain $NODE --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=300
# warmup job (pseudo)
python tools/warmup_kvcache.py --pool $POOL --tenants-file top50.txt
```

sre_oncall: @maya add the runbook steps to the maintenance ticket and ping infra-oncall 30m before start. ensure we have rollback play if BGP flaps during NIC bringup.

maya: will do. also plan to keep nvlink tracing off for the first cohort to minimize cross-node chatter.

liam: routing note — please lower batch sizes for generation routes by 10% during window to keep tail latencies bounded. and temporarily disable cheap-quant model fallbacks that increase host CPU load.

ethan: agreed on batch tuning. I'll also monitor GPU memory fragmentation metrics and trigger canary if fragmentation spike > 15%.

ops-bot: maintenance created: https://infra.redwood/maintenance/5380000001 — window THU 03:00-05:00 UTC. Automated notification will go to affected tenants 24h and 1h prior. :bell:

maya: final ask — customer-ops: please draft a short comms line highlighting low risk and cross-region fallback. i'll post in #customer-success once runbook is attached.

sre_oncall: I'll be oncall for the window. setting PagerDuty override and SOC watch. if we see >3% error-rate sustained for 5m, abort further drains and rollback.

maya: thanks all — i'll push the maintenance ticket and attach canary checklist. updating here when pre-warm jobs complete. :rocket:
